description.narrative: (USAID West Africa Regional): Despite challenges in the delivery of Family Planning (FP) services during the COVID-19 pandemic and the recent military coup in Burkina Faso, USAID's flagship FP activity continues to adapt and catalyze pathways to scaling up FP High Impact Practices (HIPs) in Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Niger and Togo. HIPs are critical to enabling countries to achieve their ambitious country-level FP goals and advancing the 2030 Ouagadougou Partnership (OP) and FP2030 targets. The OP's goal of adding 2.2 million additional FP users in the nine OP countries by 2020 was exceeded and a new ambitious target has been set to double the number of users of modern contraceptives to reach 13 million additional users by 2030. FY 2022 activities include using previous year funds to:.Conduct supportive supervision of public and non-governmental health facilities in offering FP, MCH and nutrition and integration of FP to the other maternal and child health services.Ensure the provision of essential medical equipment to selected public and non-governmental health facilities to improve quality of FP and MCH service delivery.Expand youth-led and youth-specific FP/RH activities in the 23 intervention districts.Engage and leverage domestic, donor, and West African communities and resources to build sustainability and scale of selected HIPs.Institutionalize a sustainable and self-regulating system of quality assurance. Collaborate and coordinate with other USAID FP/RH partners working on commodity security, demand creation, policy, learning, and related health systems.It will support the provision of comprehensive voluntary FP services closer to where people live in urban and peri-urban areas through facility-based, outreach mobile clinics and community based distribution of commodities. This strategy helps to reduce travel by patients to health centers thereby reducing carbon footprint from travel and help mitigate the climate impact of project activities...
